title: Forms, Labels, and Inputs
summary: Connect labels to form controls and understand form structure.

sketchBlocks.title: Use form to group controls that belong to one submission
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
A `<form>` groups the controls that belong to one user submission. The form element describes the boundary of the interaction; the controls inside it collect the values.

```html
<form>
  <label for="student-name">Name</label>
  <input id="student-name" name="student_name" type="text">
</form>
```

Read this example line by line: `form` opens the form region, the label names the field, the input collects the value, and the closing `form` ends the group. For this course, the browser preview shows the form itself; no server is required.

tryItExercises.prompt: Wrap the existing Name label and input in one form element. Keep the page heading and introduction outside the form, then confirm the field still appears in Preview.
tryItExercises.hint: The form should contain the interactive controls that belong to the same submission.

help.concept: The form element groups controls that participate in one submission.
help.hint_1: Open form immediately before the Name label.
help.hint_2: Close form immediately after the Name input.

sketchBlocks.title: Match label for with the control id
sketchBlocks.bodyMarkdown:
A visible label should be programmatically connected to its control. Give the input an `id`, then use that same value in the label's `for` attribute. This makes the label useful to mouse, touch, keyboard, and assistive-technology users.

```html
<label for="email">Email address</label>
<input id="email" name="email" type="email">
```

Read the example line by line: the label points to `email`, the input owns `id="email"`, and the matching values create the connection. The `name` identifies the value when form data is submitted.

tryItExercises.title: Connect a label to its input
tryItExercises.prompt: Connect the Email address label to the email input. Give the input `id="email"` and give the label `for="email"`. Keep the existing `name` and `type` attributes, then check the field in Preview.
tryItExercises.hint: The label's for value and the input's id must match exactly.

help.concept: Matching label for and input id values create an explicit accessible connection.
help.hint_2: Add `id="email"` to the input without removing its name or type.

quizDraft.title: Identify sound form structure
quizDraft.prompt: Which two statements describe useful form structure?
quizDraft.hint: Think about grouping and label connections.

help.concept: Forms group related controls, and labels should identify the controls they describe.
help.hint_1: One correct statement is about the form boundary.
help.hint_2: The other is about matching for and id values.

options: Place controls for one submission inside a form element.
Match a label's for value to the related control's id.
Use a heading instead of a label for every input.
Give every input the same id so labels are easier to write.

help.concept: A labeled control belongs inside its form boundary.
help.hint_1: The label can come before the input.
help.hint_2: The matching for/id connection appears before the closing form.
